mcq.q: Which set of three elements make up a protocol?
mcq.e: A protocol is a set of rules whose three elements are syntax, semantics and timing.

mcq.q: Which of the following is NOT a protocol?
mcq.e: A protocol is a set of rules, never hardware. HTTP, DHCP and DNS are all internet protocols.

mcq.q: Data flowing from a keyboard to the computer is an example of which transmission mode?
mcq.e: Simplex is one-way only, always; the keyboard can only send to the computer.

mcq.q: In which mode can data travel in both directions, but only one direction at a time?
mcq.e: Half duplex allows both ways but only one at a time, like a walkie-talkie.

mcq.q: Which of the following is NOT a mode of data exchange?
mcq.e: Multiplexing is sharing one medium among several signals, not a transmission mode.

mcq.q: A telephone call is an example of which transmission mode?
mcq.e: Full duplex lets both directions carry data simultaneously, as in a phone call.

mcq.q: In parallel transmission, data is sent as:
o: Multiple bits simultaneously over several pathways
One bit at a time over a single path
Only one direction at a time
mcq.e: Parallel transmission uses multiple pathways to send many bits at once; serial sends bits one by one.

mcq.q: What does a multiplexer do?
o: Combines many low-speed lines into one high-speed line
Splits one high-speed line into many low-speed lines
mcq.e: A multiplexer combines low-speed lines into one high-speed line; the demultiplexer reverses this.

mcq.q: The bandwidth of a communication channel refers to:
o: Its transmission capacity, i.e. data it can carry per second
How fast a signal travels through it
The loss of signal power along it
The number of devices attached to it
mcq.e: Bandwidth is channel capacity, not signal propagation speed.

mcq.q: A periodic analog signal (sine wave) is fully described by all of these EXCEPT:
mcq.e: A sine wave is defined by amplitude, frequency and phase; wavelength is derived.

mcq.q: The wavelength of a signal equals:
mcq.e: Wavelength = propagation speed x period = propagation speed / frequency.

mcq.q: Attenuation of a signal means:
o: Loss of energy as the signal propagates
Change in the shape of the signal
Sharing of a medium by several signals
mcq.e: Attenuation is loss of power; distortion changes shape; noise is unwanted addition.

mcq.q: Representing bits by changing the frequency of the carrier while keeping its amplitude constant is called:
mcq.e: FM varies the carrier frequency; AM varies its height (amplitude).

mcq.q: Pulse Code Modulation (PCM) is used to:
o: Convert an analog signal into a digital bit stream
Convert a digital signal into a sine wave
mcq.e: PCM samples, quantises and encodes an analog signal into digital bits.

mcq.q: A 10 Mbps token ring uses differential Manchester encoding. At what signalling rate does it run?
mcq.e: Manchester has a mid-bit transition, so pulse widths halve and the signalling rate doubles to 20 Mbaud.

mcq.q: A channel has 3 kHz bandwidth and a signal-to-noise ratio of 30 dB (power ratio 1000). Its Shannon capacity is approximately:
mcq.e: C = 3000 x log2(1001) is about 3000 x 10 = 30 kbps.

mcq.q: Which of the following is NOT a guided (wired) medium?
mcq.e: Infrared is wireless (unguided); the other three confine the signal inside a physical conductor.

mcq.q: Which of the following is NOT an unguided medium?
mcq.e: Coaxial cable is a guided medium.

mcq.q: Unshielded twisted pair cable terminates in which connector?
mcq.e: UTP Ethernet uses the 8-pin RJ45; RJ11 is the 4-pin telephone connector.

mcq.q: Coaxial cables are categorised by which type of rating?
mcq.e: Coax types are graded by RG ratings such as RG-59 and RG-6.

mcq.q: Light stays inside an optical fibre core because:
o: The core's refractive index is greater than the cladding's, causing total internal reflection
The cladding's refractive index is greater than the core's
The fibre is twisted to cancel interference
mcq.e: Core index > cladding index gives total internal reflection.

mcq.q: Which medium is the best choice where electrical interference is present?
mcq.e: Fibre carries light, not current, so it is immune to electrical interference; it is also the fastest medium.

mcq.q: Which statement about a point-to-point connection is correct?
o: It is a dedicated link between two devices and is not time-shared
It is shared by many stations
It is the link used by bus topology
It always needs a central hub
mcq.e: A point-to-point link is dedicated between two devices; shared links are multipoint.

mcq.q: Which topology requires a multipoint connection?
mcq.e: In a bus all stations share one backbone cable, a multipoint connection.

mcq.q: A network covering a city and carrying both data and voice is a:
mcq.e: A Metropolitan Area Network is a collection of LANs covering a city and can carry data and voice.

mcq.q: Which statement about WAN is correct?
o: It can communicate via satellites and microwaves and is slower than a LAN
It covers only one floor of a building
It is faster than a LAN
It is limited to a single campus
mcq.e: WANs span countries, use satellites/microwaves and are slower than LANs.

mcq.q: Which claim about a peer-to-peer network is FALSE?
o: Any peer can access any other
It suits small setups of about 10 machines
mcq.e: Peer-to-peer has no dedicated server; every computer is an equal peer.

mcq.q: In a client/server network, the central controller is the:
mcq.e: The server is the central controller and all others are clients.

mcq.q: Which topology gives each device a dedicated point-to-point link to a central controller?
mcq.e: Star connects every device to a central hub/controller by its own dedicated link.

mcq.q: Which topology has the highest reliability but needs the most ports and cabling?
mcq.e: In a mesh every device is linked to every other, giving n(n-1)/2 links.

mcq.q: Which of the following is NOT a network topology?
mcq.e: Stack is a data structure; real topologies are bus, star, ring, mesh, tree, hybrid.

mcq.q: Which switching technique needs a dedicated communication path held for the whole call?
mcq.e: Circuit switching reserves a dedicated physical path; packet switching shares links.

mcq.q: Which OSI layer is responsible for dialogue control and token management?
mcq.e: The Session layer (layer 5) manages dialogue and tokens.

mcq.q: Which OSI layer is responsible for routing?
mcq.e: Routing and logical addressing are Network layer jobs.

mcq.q: Which is NOT a function of the network layer?
mcq.e: Error and flow control belong to the data link and transport layers.

mcq.q: The data link layer encapsulates what it receives from the network layer into:
mcq.e: The DLL takes packets and puts them into frames.

mcq.q: Which OSI layer deals with translation, compression and encryption?
mcq.e: Presentation layer handles translation, compression and encryption.

mcq.q: Which of these layers is NOT an end-to-end (host-to-host) layer?
mcq.e: Layers 1-3 are chained (hop-by-hop); layers 4-7 are end-to-end.

mcq.q: A repeater, which regenerates a signal, operates at which layer?
mcq.e: A repeater works only in the physical layer.

mcq.q: A bridge forwarding frames from one LAN to another operates at which layer?
mcq.e: Bridges and switches work at the data link layer.

mcq.q: Which device connects networks that use different protocols and translates messages between them?
mcq.e: A gateway understands format and contents and translates; a router works at the network layer.

mcq.q: Which TCP/IP layer corresponds to the OSI Transport layer?
mcq.e: The host-to-host layer is the TCP/IP counterpart of OSI transport and holds TCP and UDP.

mcq.q: Which of these is NOT an application-layer protocol?
mcq.e: RSVP is a signalling protocol below the application layer; RTP is application-layer.

mcq.q: The Ethernet Start Frame Delimiter (SFD) is:
mcq.e: The SFD 10101011 follows the 10101010 preamble.

mcq.q: 10Base5 is also known as:
mcq.e: 10Base5 uses 500 m thick coax; 10Base2 is thin Ethernet.

mcq.q: An Ethernet has a propagation time of 25.6 microseconds and runs at 10 Mbps. The minimum frame size for CSMA/CD is:
mcq.e: 2 x 25.6 us x 10 Mbps = 512 bits = 64 bytes.

mcq.q: Token ring switches are housed in which unit?
mcq.e: The Multistation Access Unit makes the ring logically a ring but physically a star.

mcq.q: How many parity bits are needed in a Hamming code for 32 data bits?
mcq.e: Need 2^r >= m + r + 1; r = 6 gives 64 >= 39, while r = 5 gives 32 < 38.

mcq.q: Which statement about Hamming code is correct?
o: Parity bits are placed at power-of-two positions
mcq.e: Parity sits at powers of 2; Hamming corrects only a single error.

mcq.q: Which technique allows multiple packets to be sent before an acknowledgment is received?
mcq.e: Sliding window gives higher throughput than stop-and-wait.

mcq.q: How does a switched network prevent sniffing?
o: It forwards each frame only to its destination port
It broadcasts frames to all ports
mcq.e: A switch sends each frame only to the destination port.

mcq.q: Which of the following is an INVALID IPv4 address?
mcq.e: Each octet must be 0-255; 256 overflows a byte.

mcq.q: The IP address 10.231.241.1 belongs to which class?
mcq.e: First octet 1-126 means Class A.

mcq.q: Subnet mask 255.255.240.0 gives how many usable hosts per subnet?
What is the purpose of the TTL field in an IPv4 header?
o: To stop datagrams circulating forever in routing loops
mcq.e: TTL is decremented per hop and the datagram is discarded at zero.

mcq.q: Which field is NOT used for IPv4 fragmentation?
mcq.e: Fragmentation uses Identification, Flags and Fragment Offset.

mcq.q: The maximum length of an IPv4 datagram is:
mcq.e: The 16-bit total-length field limits it to 65,535 bytes.

mcq.q: DHCP is an extension of which protocol?
mcq.e: DHCP extends the bootstrap protocol and supports manual and automatic assignment.

mcq.q: APIPA self-assigned addresses fall in which range?
mcq.e: APIPA addresses are used when DHCP fails.

mcq.q: In DNS, the client is called the:
mcq.e: DNS converts domain names to IPs; its client is the resolver.

mcq.q: Which routing algorithm is described as Dijkstra-based, while distance vector uses Bellman-Ford?
mcq.e: Link state = Dijkstra; distance vector = Bellman-Ford.

mcq.q: A hierarchical network has 630 routers in 7 clusters, each of 9 regions with 10 routers. How many routing table entries does each router need?
Sending each incoming packet on every outgoing line except the one it arrived on is called:
mcq.e: Flooding is robust but wasteful and is a static algorithm.

mcq.q: Which network requires circuit setup before data transfer?
mcq.e: Virtual circuits need setup; datagram networks do not.

mcq.q: A socket is concretely made up of:
mcq.e: A socket is the IPC endpoint: IP address plus port number.

mcq.q: How many bytes is the UDP header, and which field does it lack that TCP has?
mcq.e: UDP has only source port, destination port, length and checksum, so no sequence number.

mcq.q: The TCP connection setup three-way handshake is:
mcq.e: The exchange SYN -> SYN-ACK -> ACK indicates successful establishment.

mcq.q: In TCP, the acknowledgement number indicates:
mcq.e: ACK is cumulative and names the next byte expected.

mcq.q: A TCP segment with the RST flag set causes:
o: A clean close with FIN and ACK
mcq.e: RST aborts the connection at once.

mcq.q: During TCP slow start, the congestion window approximately:
mcq.e: Slow start is exponential; congestion avoidance adds 1 MSS per RTT.

mcq.q: Which port number is used by IMAP?
mcq.e: IMAP = 143; SMTP 25, DNS 53, HTTP 80.

mcq.q: Which of these is the FALSE characteristic of SSL?
o: It works between the network and transport layer
It operates above the transport layer
mcq.e: SSL operates above the transport layer, not between network and transport.

mcq.q: HTTP is called a stateless protocol because:
o: It keeps no memory between requests
mcq.e: HTTP runs on TCP port 80 and keeps no state; cookies add state.

mcq.q: FTP uses which ports for control and data?
mcq.e: Control port 21, data port 20.

mcq.q: Which RTSP state means the server breaks down the connection and frees resources?
mcq.e: TEARDOWN ends the session and frees resources.

mcq.q: Which protocol is the EDI protocol for electronic data interchange between businesses?
mcq.e: X.12 is EDI; X.25 is DTE/DCE; XMPP is IM; XMODEM is file transfer.

mcq.q: Which protocol carries real-time audio and video multimedia?
mcq.e: RTP carries real-time multimedia content.

mcq.q: Which IEEE standard is the WLAN security standard from which WPA2 comes?
mcq.e: 802.11i is WLAN security; 802.3 is wired Ethernet.

mcq.q: Which is the correct ascending order of speed?
mcq.e: Speed order is GSM, GPRS, EDGE, LTE.

mcq.q: Bluetooth 5.0 has a maximum speed of:
mcq.e: Bluetooth 5.0 = 2 Mbps, double 4.x.

mcq.q: Which entity informs the HLR of a mobile station's location changes?
mcq.e: The VLR informs the HLR.

mcq.q: Which is NOT a location-update scheme in mobile networks?
mcq.e: The notes list periodic, movement-based and distance-based only.

mcq.q: IPSec tunnel mode protects:
mcq.e: Tunnel mode protects the whole packet; transport mode only the payload.

mcq.q: The key sizes of DES, Triple DES and IDEA respectively are:
mcq.e: DES 56, 3DES 168, IDEA 128 bits.

mcq.q: Which of the following is NOT a symmetric-key algorithm?
mcq.e: RSA is asymmetric (public key).

mcq.q: A digital signature is created using:
mcq.e: Sign with sender's private key; verify with sender's public key.

mcq.q: The man-in-the-middle attack on Diffie-Hellman is called:
mcq.e: The bucket brigade attack is the Diffie-Hellman MITM.

mcq.q: Which of these is NOT a DoS attack?
mcq.e: Code Red is a worm.

mcq.q: What is the most common IDS detection method?
mcq.e: Signature-based detection matches known attack patterns.

mcq.q: A virus that corrupts the partition table makes the hard disk:
mcq.e: Corrupting the FAT only loses files; the partition table makes the disk inaccessible.

mcq.q: In a reverse auction:
o: The buyer posts a need and sellers bid successively lower
Sellers post items and buyers bid higher
mcq.e: Sellers bid lower until one remains.

mcq.q: A VPN is best described as:
o: A private network using a public network to connect remote sites or users
mcq.e: VPN traffic is tunnelled and encrypted over public networks.

mcq.q: Which network first initiated the internet and first used packet switching?
mcq.e: ARPANET, 1969.

tf.s: Half duplex allows data in both directions simultaneously.
tf.n: Half duplex is both ways but only one at a time; full duplex is simultaneous.

tf.s: A sine wave is described by amplitude, frequency and phase.
tf.n: Wavelength is derived, not a defining parameter.

tf.s: Optical fibre is a guided medium.
tf.n: It confines light inside the fibre.

tf.s: Peer-to-peer networks require a dedicated server.
tf.n: Peer-to-peer has no dedicated server; all peers are equal.

tf.s: Packet switching is used by ARPANET and the internet.
tf.n: Circuit switching needs a dedicated path.

tf.s: Layers 1-3 of OSI are end-to-end and layers 4-7 are chained.
tf.n: Reversed: layers 1-3 are chained, layers 4-7 end-to-end.

tf.s: A router operates at the network layer.
tf.n: It connects multiple networks and uses routing tables.

tf.s: Hamming code can correct multiple errors.
tf.n: It corrects a single error only.

tf.s: In IPv4 translation to IPv6 headers, the flow label is considered.
tf.n: The flow label has no IPv4 counterpart and is not considered.

tf.s: Link state routing uses the Bellman-Ford algorithm.
tf.n: Link state uses Dijkstra; distance vector uses Bellman-Ford.
It sends datagrams without establishing a connection.

tf.s: SSL operates between the network and transport layers.
tf.n: SSL operates above the transport layer.

tf.s: A certificate contains the owner's private key.
tf.n: It contains the public key, owner information and validity period.

The data unit of the transport layer is called a ______.
A mesh network of n devices has n(n-1)/2 ______.
The TCP three-way handshake is SYN, SYN-ACK and ______.
The default HTTP port number is ______.
A subnet mask of 255.255.240.0 allows ______ usable hosts.
______ stands for Classless Inter Domain Routing.
The three security goals are Confidentiality, Integrity and ______.
